payload.excerpt: A wedding morning timeline worked back from your ceremony: when hair and makeup start, who sits first and last, when the photographer arrives and where the buffer goes, with a sample morning for a 4pm ceremony.
key_takeaways: Start from the ceremony time and work backwards through travel, photos and dressing to find when the first chair must begin, which in our 4pm example is 9am with a first look or 10am without one.
The number of people in the chairs, and the pace your stylist and artist give you at the trial, set the start time.
The person getting married sits last or close to last, so their hair and makeup are freshest for the photos.
Put the buffer before dressing and before you leave for the ceremony, not spread thinly across the morning.

faq.q: How early do bridesmaids get ready?
faq.a: Early enough for every chair to finish before dressing. Bridesmaids sit before the person getting married, so the first chair of the morning may be theirs: 9am in our 4pm example with a first look, or 10am without one.

faq.q: What time should hair and makeup start for a 4pm ceremony?
faq.a: In our examples, 9am with a first look and 10am without one. Your own start depends on the number of people getting ready, so ask your stylist and artist to work back from your dressed-by time.

faq.q: Should the bride go first or last in hair and makeup?
faq.a: Last, or close to last, so hair and makeup are freshest for the photos. Some teams place the person getting married second to last, so an overrun falls on someone else.

faq.q: What time should the photographer arrive on the wedding morning?
faq.a: While the last chair is still in progress, leaving time for details before dressing. In our 4pm examples, that is 12.30pm with a first look and 1.30pm without one.

faq.q: How much buffer should you leave on the wedding morning?
faq.a: Put it at the handovers: before the dress goes on, before you leave and around a first look. For example, leave 15 minutes between the last chair and dressing.
